thread:
maria_sec: FYI AegisEdge (vendor) just pinged about a potential S3 credential exposure in one of their CI pipelines. They posted an incident page: https://status.aegisedge.com/incidents/42. Can we do a quick impact check for Redwood? cc @ashish_oncall @tom_ciso

ashish_oncall: On it. Which Redwood services talk to AegisEdge? I think telemetry ingest and the metrics exporter. @leo_infra do you have a mapping?

leo_infra: Confirmed: integrations exist for redwood-telemetry-prod and model-metrics-proxy. Keys are service-account style API keys and an IAM role used by the metrics exporter. I’ll start pulling the last 24h access logs and list active keys.

sam_aegis: (AegisEdge) We're isolating the offending pipeline run and rotating any tokens we see in CI. Root cause appears to be an accidentally checked-in env file in a transient container. No signs yet of external downloads outside our infra. Will provide timeline in ~15m.

maria_sec: Quick action plan: 1) Rotate any AegisEdge API keys used by Redwood now 2) Revoke related IAM keys/tokens 3) Export audit logs for those two services and search for unknown IPs/user-agents 4) Prep comms if we find customer data. I'll coordinate rotations — please report status here.

leo_infra: Running log query now: `aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/lambda/telemetry --start-time $(date -d '24 hours ago' +%s)000` — streaming results. Also listing active access keys for the integration user.

ash_sre: Suggest immediate containment: deny inbound calls from AegisEdge principal until rotations complete. Temporary SCP/deny policy or revoke session tokens. I'll draft a deny policy and hold off on blanket account lockdown to avoid service outage.

sam_aegis: Update: revoked the leaked CI token and disabled the pipeline agent. We isolated the build host and rotated internal credentials. Our logs show only internal AegisEdge IPs accessed the S3 object; no external actor has fetched the file so far. Full timeline & hash of artifact will be posted in 30m.

tom_ciso: Please provide the exact timestamp when tokens were revoked and copies of relevant logs (or signed attestations). If there's any chance of PII exposure we need to loop Legal.

maria_sec: Keys rotated on our side for the two integrations (redwood-telemetry-prod, model-metrics-proxy). Revoked the associated IAM access keys and forced new service tokens. Initial audit shows reads only from internal AWS IP ranges, no suspicious GETs. Opening a post-incident ticket to cover: RBAC review, KMS key grant audit, and CI secrets hygiene. Next steps: 1) get AegisEdge RCA 2) update onboarding docs to ban embedding creds in CI artifacts 3) ensure KMS grants are not granted to ephemeral build roles. tagging @security-team for follow-up.

incident-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026-072 and assigned to maria_sec, due in 7 days.

sam_aegis: We'll share the RCA doc and a signed attestation by EOD. Thanks for the fast coordination and for rotating keys quickly.
